questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some pens are boxes.

No box is a fan.

Some pens are fans.

**Conclusions:**

I. No pen is a fan.

Il. No box is a pen.

III. Some fans are pens.

IV. Some boxes are pens.

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions Il and IV follow
Only conclusions I and Il follow
Only conclusions Ill and IV follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5df61a7ee19b23e2ed2b001d881b7a60332ab01d7b6c2acbc45ba905bfba4d48.png] 

Conclusions:

I. No pen is a fan → Does not Follow (As, no box is a fan and some pens are fans. So, no direct negative or cross relation is given between pens and fan therefore it is definitely false)

II. No box is a pen → Does not Follow (As, some pens are boxes and no box is a fan. So, no direct negative or cross relation is given between pens and box therefore it is definitely false)

III. Some fans are pens → Follow (As, some pens are fans. So, as some part of pens is common with fans therefore it is definitely true.)

IV. Some boxes are pens → Follow (As, some pens are boxes. So, as some part of pens is common with boxes therefore it is definitely true.)

So, Only conclusions Ill and IV follow.

Hence, the correct answer is "**Only conclusions Ill and IV follow**".

questions.question: Intensive agriculture implies ______.

options.text: cultivating large farms with moderately low inputs of labour and capital
use of more labour and capital inputs on the given land under cultivation
spreading farming across more states of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**use of more labour and capital inputs on the given land under cultivation.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Intensive agriculture, also known as** intensive farming**, maximizes agricultural production from a given area of land using **higher inputs of labour, machinery, and other farming resources.**
 
• This method represents a stark contrast to **extensive farming**, where the **land is used more broadly with less management or fewer inputs per unit area.**
 
• Intensive agriculture uses practices like **irrigation, advanced fertilizers, and other technological inputs** to **generate a high output per unit of land,** making it well-suited for regions with high population density where land is in short supply.
 
• **The aim** of this agricultural practice is **to grow plentiful crops and raise large numbers of animals cheaply and rapidly,** which often leads to higher environmental impact compared to less intensive farming systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Extensive Farming:**

 
 
• Extensive farming is characterized by **low inputs of labour and capital** per unit area of land.
 
• This farming method is traditionally used in **regions with low agricultural productivity, such as remote, mountainous, or dry regions**, where arable land is abundant.
 
• It has** less of an impact on the environment **per unit of area compared to intensive farming, as **it tends not to employ large amounts of harmful fertilizers or pesticides.**
 
• However, it usually **generates less production per unit of land,** which can be a potential downside in areas where the population is growing and food demand is high.
 
 
 
• **Mechanized Farming:**
 
 
• Mechanized farming is characterized by the** use of machinery for various farming operations**, replacing traditional manual and animal labour.
 
• This type of farming is usually employed in developed countries and in places** where the cost of labour is high or labour is scarce.**
 
• Mechanized farming significantly **increases the efficiency and productivity** of the land, making large-scale farming feasible.
 
• On the downside,** it requires significant investment in machinery,** which can be a barrier for small-scale farmers.
 
 
 
• **Diversified Farming:**
 
 
• Diversified farming involves **growing a variety of crops or raising various types of livestock on the same farm** to maximize output and reduce risk.
 
• This type of agriculture **provides a variety of products, promoting food security,** and can help to **safeguard against the failure of a single crop** or livestock.
 
• Diversified farming can be **beneficial to the environment, promoting biodiversity** and reducing the need for chemical inputs as different plants and livestock can help to control pests and replenish soil nutrients.
 
• However, it can** require more labour, knowledge, and management** compared to monocultures due to the complexity of farming multiple crops or livestock types.

questions.question: Nana Sahib, a rebel at Kanpur was the son of which of the following Peshwas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Baji Rao ll.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nana Sahib**, born as **Dhondu Pant,** was an Indian Peshwa (prime minister) of the **Maratha empire.**
 
• He was **adopted by Baji Rao II**, who was the **last Peshwa of the Maratha Empire.**
 
• Nana Sahib played a **significant role in the Indian Rebellion of 1857** (also known as the First War of Independence or the Sepoy Mutiny).
 
• He led the revolt in the region of** Kanpur (Cawnpore) **and despite initial successes, **was defeated by British forces **later on.
 
• After the Indian rebellion, he disappeared, and his ultimate fate was never known, leading to various theories and speculations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baji Rao I**:

questions.question: What helps making the acidic food alkaline that is coming from the stomach?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bile juice.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bile juice is secreted by the liver and stored in the gallbladder. It is released into the small intestine when food enters.
 
• Bile neutralizes the acid in chyme, raising its pH and making the intestinal environment more alkaline.
 
• This is a critical step, as the enzymes in the small intestine that further digest food work optimally in an alkaline condition.
 
• Along with neutralizing the acid, bile aids in the emulsification of dietary fat, which helps in its digestion.
 
• It's important to note that excessive bile or reflux of bile into the stomach can cause discomfort and affect the digestive process.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pepsin:
 
 
• Pepsin is an enzyme that is released in the stomach to break down proteins into smaller peptides during digestion.
 
• It is produced by the chief cells in the stomach lining and is activated by the acidic environment of the stomach.
 
• Pepsin is not involved in making food alkaline, instead, it assists in further breaking down food particles.
 
• Faulty regulation or overproduction of pepsin can lead to peptic ulcers or other gastric disorders.
 
 
 
• Gastric Juice:
 
 
• Gastric juice, a combination of pepsin, hydrochloric acid, and other enzymes, is secreted into the stomach to aid in the digestion of food.
 
• It is acidic in nature, with a pH ranging from 1.5 to 3.5, which is essential for pepsin's protein digestion process.
 
• The acidity of gastric juice also kills many bacteria that enter the stomach, providing a protective function against infection.
 
• Gastric juice is not responsible for making food alkaline, but rather for launching the initial stages of digestion in a highly acidic environment.
 
 
 
• Hydrochloric Acid:
 
 
• Hydrochloric acid (HCl) is one of the main components of gastric juice.
 
• It creates the acidic environment in the stomach needed to activate pepsin and other enzymes.
 
• HCl helps to break down food and kill ingested pathogens.
 
• Like pepsin and gastric juice, hydrochloric acid participates in digestion within the stomach, but it does not play a part in making the chyme alkaline.

• Ashoka's emblem of the **"Lion Capital" **atop the **Ashoka Pillar at Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh, India,** is adopted as the **National Emblem of India**.

questions.question: 15 men and 21 women, working together, can do a job in 56 days, while 12 men and 24 women, working together, can do the same job in 64 days. In how many days can the same job be done by 18 men and 24 women, working together?

Total work = efficiency × time

Total Simple Interest percentage = (3 ÷ 5) × 100 = 60%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c83b0ae8cac415066ebd2fb6682632b4c893a8f081ab948cacb5eadbf1765884.png]

⇒ (3 ÷ 5) × P = (P × R × 12) ÷ 100

⇒ 3 ÷ 5 = (12 × R) ÷ 100

⇒ R = (3 × 100) ÷ (5 × 12)

⇒ R = 300 ÷ 60

⇒ R = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5% p.a.**

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is strictly calculated only on the principal amount, whereas Compound Interest is calculated on the principal amount as well as the accumulated interest from previous periods.

Difference between CI and SI

Compound Interest Formula
